$comment: Generated by scripts/sync-tools.mjs from a Bytebase instance's built-in MCP server. Do not edit by hand; rerun `npm run sync-tools`.

tools.name: call_api
tools.description:
Execute a Bytebase API endpoint. **Use search_api first to get operationId and schema.**

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| operationId | Yes | e.g., "SQLService/Query" |
| body | No | JSON request body |

**Resource names:** Preserve the exact canonical name returned by ListDatabases:
instances/prod/databases/main for a workspace instance, or
projects/my-project/instances/prod/databases/main for a project instance.

**Example:**
call_api(operationId="SQLService/Query", body={"name": "projects/my-project/instances/i/databases/db", "statement": "SELECT 1"})

tools.name: decide_issue
tools.description:
Approve or reject a Bytebase issue at its current approval step. The user confirms the decision in this client first.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| issue     | Yes      | Issue name, e.g. "projects/hr/issues/42" |
| decision  | Yes      | "approve" or "reject" |
| comment   | No       | Note recorded with the decision |

The tool shows the user what the issue changes and asks them to confirm in a form. It decides only when they accept; declining or cancelling changes nothing. A client that cannot show the form gets the issue's link, to decide it in the Bytebase console instead. Do not ask in chat first: the form is the question.

It decides database changes and access requests. Role requests stay in the Bytebase console, because approving one grants a project role.

The approval rules decide who may approve, as in the console: the user must hold the role of the current step, and approving their own issue, or a plan they last changed, is refused unless the project allows it.

This is the only way to decide an issue over MCP; call_api refuses IssueService/ApproveIssue and RejectIssue.

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description:
Inspect a Bytebase database's schema.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| database  | Yes      | Database name or substring (e.g., "employee_db" or "employee") |
| instance  | No       | Workspace instance ID/name, or the full canonical name for a project instance |
| project   | No       | Project name or ID to narrow resolution |
| schema    | No       | Schema name for multi-schema engines (PG/MSSQL/Oracle/Snowflake/Redshift/CockroachDB/Databricks/Trino/Spanner/Hive); ignored with a note on MySQL/TiDB/etc. |
| table     | No       | Drill into a single table; implies include="details" |
| include   | No       | Detail level: "summary" (default), "columns", "details" |

**Usage:**
- First call: get_schema(database="employee") → compact overview
- Drill down: get_schema(database="employee", table="orders") → full table detail
- Write a query: get_schema(database="employee", include="columns") → all tables with columns

**Notes:**
- Metadata is auto-synced on access. The first call to a stale database may take longer.
- For databases with many tables, columns/details modes return up to 200 tables PER SCHEMA.
  Use schema= or table= to narrow further.
- Column masking metadata is only returned when table= is set.
- Requires bb.databases.getSchema permission.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description:
Get step-by-step guides for Bytebase tasks.

**Tip:** Use query_database for SQL queries and propose_database_change for single-database DDL/DML — they handle resolution automatically.

**Workflow:** get_skill("task") → search_api(operationId) → call_api(...)

Skills: query, database-change

tools.name: grant_masking_exemption
tools.description:
Exempt one member from data masking in a Bytebase project, for one database (optionally one schema, table or column) or for every database in the project. The user confirms the exemption in this client first.

| Parameter    | Required | Description |
|--------------|----------|-------------|
| project      | Yes      | Project name, e.g. "projects/hr" |
| member       | Yes      | "user:{email}", "group:{email}", "serviceAccount:{email}" or "workloadIdentity:{email}" |
| database     | One of   | Database name, e.g. "instances/prod/databases/hr"; it must belong to the project |
| allDatabases | One of   | true for every database in the project, current and future |
| schema       | No       | Narrow to one schema (needs database) |
| table        | No       | Narrow to one table (needs database) |
| column       | No       | Narrow to one column (needs table) |
| expireTime   | No       | RFC 3339 time the exemption ends, e.g. "2026-10-27T00:00:00Z"; without it, it does not expire |
| reason       | No       | Why, recorded with the exemption |

An exemption is a standing policy change: the member then sees the covered data unmasked in query and export results. For a one-off query, request an access grant instead (AccessGrantService/CreateAccessGrant).

The tool adds one exemption and leaves every other entry as it is. It shows the user the member, the scope, the expiry and the effect, and asks them to confirm in a form; it writes only when they accept. A client that cannot show the form gets the project's masking exemption page, to grant it in the Bytebase console instead. Do not ask in chat first: the form is the question.

The same permissions apply as in the console. This and revoke_masking_exemption are the only ways to change exemptions over MCP; call_api refuses OrgPolicyService/UpdatePolicy.

tools.name: propose_database_change
tools.description:
Run DDL/DML changes (ALTER TABLE, CREATE TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE, migrations) against a Bytebase database.

This is the primary tool for making database changes. Use this instead of manually calling CreateSheet/CreatePlan/CreateIssue via call_api.

Provide plain SQL — the tool handles database resolution, sheet creation, plan creation with automatic plan checks, and issue creation in one call. Optionally creates a rollout.

| Parameter     | Required | Description |
|---------------|----------|-------------|
| database      | Yes      | Database name or substring |
| sql           | Yes      | SQL statement(s) in plain text (NOT base64) |
| title         | Yes      | Title for the issue/plan |
| instance      | No       | Workspace instance ID/name, or the full canonical name for a project instance |
| project       | No       | Project name or ID to narrow resolution |
| changeType    | No       | "MIGRATE" (default) or "SDL" |
| createRollout | No       | If true, attempts rollout creation after issue |
| reason        | No       | Context or ticket reference (max 1000 chars) |

**Examples:**
propose_database_change(database="app", sql="ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(20)", title="Add status column")
propose_database_change(database="app", sql="UPDATE orders SET status='shipped' WHERE id=42", title="Ship order 42", createRollout=true)

**Notes:**
- v1 supports single database targets only. For batch changes across multiple databases, use get_skill("database-change").
- Plan checks run automatically; results included in response when available.
- Requires bb.sheets.create, bb.plans.create, bb.issues.create permissions.
- If createRollout=true but policy gates aren't satisfied, returns success with rolloutCreated=false and a reason.
- nextAction AWAIT_HUMAN_APPROVAL means the issue waits for its approvers. If the user is one of them, decide_issue asks them to confirm in this client and then approves; otherwise share links.issue with an approver.
- Masked data: a masked column reads back as "******". That is a placeholder, not a value anything holds. Any change containing it is refused, because writing it back would overwrite the real value. Ask a human to make the change in the Bytebase console instead.

tools.name: query_database
tools.description:
Execute a SQL query against a Bytebase database. Resolves the database by name automatically.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| database  | Yes      | Database name or substring (e.g., "employee_db" or "employee") |
| statement | Yes      | SQL query to execute |
| instance  | No       | Workspace instance ID/name, or the full canonical name for a project instance |
| project   | No       | Project name or ID to narrow resolution |
| schema    | No       | Default schema for unqualified names (Postgres search path). An access grant applies only when this equals the grant's schema |
| container | No       | CosmosDB container (required for CosmosDB). An access grant applies only when this equals the grant's container |
| limit     | No       | Max rows (default: 100, max: 1000) |

**Examples:**
query_database(database="employee_db", statement="SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 10")
query_database(database="employee", instance="prod-pg", statement="SELECT count(*) FROM orders")
query_database(database="employee", instance="projects/hr/instances/prod-pg", statement="SELECT count(*) FROM orders")

**Notes:**
- Masked data: masking replaces a value fully (by default "******"), partly (e.g. "**rn**"), or with a hash. maskedColumns in the result names each masked column and why (not reported for MongoDB, CosmosDB or Elasticsearch). A masked value is a placeholder, not a value anything holds, so never write it back and never filter on it. Any statement containing "******" is refused. When showing a partly masked value, wrap it in backticks: "**rn**" renders as bold Markdown.
- Seeing masked values: the user can ask a project owner for a masking exemption, or, if the project allows just-in-time access, request an access grant with Unmask for this exact statement, schema and container. In a Read-write session, file the request with call_api(operationId="AccessGrantService/CreateAccessGrant"); otherwise the user requests it in the SQL Editor. Once it is approved, find the grant among the user's access grants, then rerun the granted statement unchanged with the grant's schema and container. appliedAccessGrant in the result names the grant that applied.

tools.name: reauthorize
tools.description:
Log out the current MCP OAuth connection so the client can run OAuth again.

Use this when you need to change the connected Bytebase account or SaaS workspace. After this tool succeeds, retry the MCP request or reconnect; the server will return the normal OAuth challenge.

tools.name: revoke_masking_exemption
tools.description:
Remove one member's masking exemption in a Bytebase project. The user confirms in this client first.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| project   | Yes      | Project name, e.g. "projects/hr" |
| member    | Yes      | The member as the policy lists it, e.g. "user:bob@example.com" |
| condition | Yes      | The exemption's condition expression, exactly as OrgPolicyService/GetPolicy returns it for "{project}/policies/masking_exemption"; "" for an exemption with no condition |

The member is removed from every exemption whose condition matches exactly; an exemption left with no member is removed. Other members and other exemptions stay as they are. The tool asks the user to confirm in a form, and writes only when they accept. A client that cannot show the form gets the project's masking exemption page.

The same permissions apply as in the console.

tools.name: search_api
tools.description:
Discover Bytebase API endpoints. **Always call before call_api - never guess schemas.**

| Mode | Parameters | Result |
|------|------------|--------|
| List | (none) | All services |
| Browse | service="SQLService" | All endpoints in service |
| Details | operationId="SQLService/Query" | Request/response schema |
| Schema | schema="Instance" | Message type definition |

**Workflow:** search_api() → search_api(service="...") → search_api(operationId="...") → call_api(...)

tools.name: set_just_in_time_access
tools.description:
Turn just-in-time access on or off for one Bytebase project. The user confirms the change in this client first.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| project   | Yes      | Project name, e.g. "projects/hr" |
| enabled   | Yes      | true to turn it on, false to turn it off |

Just-in-time access lets members request access grants in the project: time-boxed permission to run one statement, for a one-off query. With it off, new requests are refused, and active grants stop applying until it is turned on again; they are not revoked.

The tool shows the user the change and asks them to confirm in a form. It changes the setting only when they accept; declining or cancelling changes nothing. A client that cannot show the form gets the project's settings link, to change it in the Bytebase console instead. Do not ask in chat first: the form is the question.

Changing it needs bb.projects.update, as in the console. This is the only way to change it over MCP; call_api refuses ProjectService/UpdateProject.
